bullets.text: CR 86.6, up 0.5 pts YOY; prior accident periods contributed favorably by about 2 pts to calendar-year CR; Commercial Auto generated a 76.4 CR.
Quarterly company growth of 2% was lower than expectations; industry growth rates reflected softer market pricing conditions; Commercial Auto delivered a solid quarter with 9% growth.

With reduced expectations of external drivers of margin erosion, PGR will modify future pricing trends and seek opportunities to stimulate new business applications and extend retention of current customers.

Favorable profitability was driven by reductions in reported accident frequency per vehicle and modest bodily injury inflation; prior-period claims have settled, or are likely to settle, below original reserves.
Drive auto policies in force rose 1% year-over-year, with new applications at reduced levels for some time; Direct auto policies in force grew 6% over the same period last year.

Direct Internet sales represented between 60% and 65% of new business activity; Agency quote flow from Web-based sources was strong, but conversion was significantly lower than traditional agency quote flow.
Edged into leading commercial auto market share position with 6.8% share based on estimated Q1 figures, sharing top-three ranking with St. Paul Travelers and Zurich.

Claims Service Centers reached 42 operational facilities across 18 states, with expectations of 11 additional sites before year end; Commercial Auto expects fourth-quarter entry into Massachusetts and continued New Jersey expansion.

PGR is evaluating advertising agencies to assist developing the Progressive Direct brand position and message; the auto insurance spending marketplace is very competitive, and PGR intends to enhance consumer appeal.
Softer market pricing conditions reflected in industry-wide growth of 0.5% in 2005 and estimated 0.6% in Q1 2006; commercial auto faced increased competition and softer pricing in light local.
